You are the Explainer for a team of specialists who reviewed a Magic: The Gathering limited card pool for a player. You are given the three best decks that code built from the pool, ranked by code, and the specialists' findings. Write the review's summary for the player.

Rules:
1. Do not change the ranking. The decks are ranked by a score that code computed. Explain it; do not reorder or replace a deck.
2. Restate, do not invent. Every claim you make rests on a finding you were given or on the decks as printed. Do not add numbers; if you quote one, copy it from a finding.
3. Cite cards. Every note names the pool cards it is about, by their exact names. A note with no card, or a card not in the pool, is thrown away.
4. The verdict is for a player at a table: say which deck to register and why, in at most four sentences, then the one or two things to watch.
5. Report disagreements. When two specialists' findings pull against each other (one wants a color, another says it is thin), list the disagreement with both agents' ids, the cards involved and what decides it. Do not average them away. If there is no disagreement, return an empty list.
6. Answer with one JSON object and nothing else, in the schema below.

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else:
{
  "confidence": <number from 0 to 1>,
  "verdict": "<at most four sentences>",
  "decks": [ { "rank": <1, 2 or 3>, "note": "<one or two sentences>", "cards": ["<exact card name>", ...] } ],
  "disagreements": [ { "topic": "<short>", "agents": ["<agent id>", "<agent id>"], "cards": ["<exact card name>", ...], "note": "<one or two sentences>" } ]
}

request.cachedContext:
# Pool bundle
Set: trk (Star Trek), format speed: medium, brief version 1
Speed notes: Speed varies by archetype. B/R Klingons and R/W Command want to end the game early with haste and wide boards, while U/B, W/U, and G/U play longer games as Spacecraft, modal spells, and land counts come online. Treat this as a starting point until real prerelease results arrive.
Grades are 0.0 to 5.0 in half steps, relative to this set; 5.0 is the best.

## Set mechanics
- Surveil: Surveil N means "Look at the top N cards of your library, then put any number of them into your graveyard and the rest on top of your library in any order."
- Station: Station is an activated ability of Spacecraft: "Tap another creature you control: Put charge counters equal to its power on this permanent. Activate only as a sorcery." Each striation, such as 6+, grants its abilities once the permanent has that many charge counters, and a striation with a power and toughness makes it an artifact creature.
- Strange new worlds: Strange new worlds is an ability word. Its abilities count the number of differently named lands you control.
- Beam me up: Beam me up [cost] means "You may cast this card from your graveyard by paying [cost] and returning a creature you control to its owner's hand. If you do, exile it as it leaves the stack." It appears on instants and sorceries, and normal timing rules still apply.
- Landfall: Landfall is an ability word. Its abilities trigger whenever a land enters the battlefield under your control, whether it was played or put there by an effect.
- Face a dilemma: You face a dilemma whenever you choose one or more modes for a modal spell or ability. Choosing several modes is still one dilemma. "Whenever you face a dilemma" triggers resolve before the spell or ability that caused them.
- Federation: Federation is an ability word. Its abilities count the number of creature types among non-Borg creatures you control.
- Assimilate: To assimilate a creature or creature card, put it onto the battlefield under your control, or gain control of it, with a +1/+1 counter. It becomes a Borg artifact creature and loses all other creature types.

## Designed archetypes
- WU Spacecraft and Artificers: Play creatures with useful enters effects, then tap them to station Spacecraft. Hold the board while the ships come online over a turn or two. Signposts: Constable Odo; Hemmer, Fixing What Is Broken. Key commons: Interstellar Effigy.
- UB Dilemma Control: Choose between proactive and reactive modes on modal spells to stay in control, then win with cards that pay off each time you face a dilemma. Signposts: Lore, Positronic Provocateur; Seven of Nine. Key commons: Consider the Prime Directive.
- BR Klingons and Dies: Attack with hasty Klingon Warrior tokens, then sacrifice them or let them die for value. Some creatures want to die. Signposts: The Duras Sisters; L'Rell, Fierce Visionary. Key commons: A Good Day to Die; Starfleet Security.
- RG Away Team Landfall: Put lands onto the battlefield as often as possible and turn each landfall trigger into damage or bigger creatures. Trigger doublers make it explosive. Signposts: Cleveland Booker, Empath; Dal R'El, Augment Orphan.
- WG Doctors and Counters: Grow creatures with +1/+1 counters. Payoffs that care about any kind of counter also count the charge counters on Spacecraft. Signposts: The Doctor, EMH; Phlox, Unorthodox Doctor. Key commons: Pure Energy.
- WB Borg Artifact Creatures: Build a board of Borg artifact creatures, pump them together, and sacrifice artifacts you no longer need for bigger effects. Signposts: Locutus, the One Who Speaks; Zero, Incorporeal Sensate. Key commons: Vexing Drone; Assault Drone.
- UR Scientists and Noncreatures: Cast cheap noncreature spells every turn to trigger Scientist payoffs. Spacecraft count as noncreature spells when cast. Signposts: Gray and Adira, Forever Joined; Spock, Always Your Friend.
- BG Archaeology Graveyard: Fill the graveyard with creatures and artifacts, surveil every turn, and bring the best cards back with reanimation and beam me up spells. Signposts: Daniels, Temporal Agent; Vash, Freelance Archaeologist. Key commons: Pattern Buffer Preservation.
- RW Command: Go wide with Officer tokens until your creatures total 8 or more power, then use the command payoffs to break through blockers. Signposts: Kirk, Commanding Officer; Worf, Honor-Bound Warrior.
- UG Strange New Worlds: Play as many differently named lands as you can, including Planets and Anomalies. Off-color Planets are worth playing for their life gain and to power up strange new worlds cards. Signposts: D'Vana Tendi, Optimistic Ensign; The Traveler. Key commons: Suus Mahna Practitioner; Orion; Risa.

## Generic archetypes
None.
